correctness.rationale: The plane cubic divisor/conic equivalence is proved with line bundles O_E(6O), and reducibility corresponds exactly to partition into zero-sum collinear triples. The three Frobenius cases follow from the explicit model Y^2=X^3-432, the cubic-residue condition on two-torsion and the rational flexes constituting three-torsion. A characteristic-independent enumeration covers every one of the 296010 six-subsets of the 27-element torsion set, verifying the 8244/2268/5976 totals and their full orbit cycles. Independently, the proof counts 36 fixed conics in the three-cycle case, 76 in the involution case and 54 fixed reducible ones in the latter; the new smooth counts 0 and 22 follow. Two standalone verifiers run on final scientific paths and test finite-field coordinate examples and exhaustive group combinatorics. No inference from a finite-field sample to every prime is used.

value.rationale: For an established canonical 8244-conic incidence configuration, the complete arithmetic Frobenius and geometric irreducibility classification over every characteristic >=5 finite field is a nontrivial natural invariant, especially the dichotomy of zero or 22 rational smooth six-point conics in nonsplit cases. Rational line incidence and conic zeta functions provide explicit extension-field data. The result goes substantially beyond re-counting 8244 complex conics or merely evaluating a single small characteristic, and may guide further arithmetic studies of osculating arrangements.
